title: What You Can't See Is What You Learn: Restricted Evidence Visibility Favors Compositional Generalization in Shared-Genome Language-Model Societies
abstract: arXiv:2608.20054v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Multi-module systems often expose every module to the full input. We test whether restricting evidence visibility changes which solutions gradient-based training discovers. Four-cell societies share one frozen pretrained language model and one low-rank adapter, communicating only through two model-width continuous vectors in a fixed relay. On a prospectively sealed natural-language function-composition task, we train ten matched restricted/global pairs sharing initialization bytes, training order, token layout, parameters, and computation; only the attention mask differs. Restricted societies outperform their globally visible twins by at least 20 points at both depths in 9 of 10 pairs, with median paired advantages of 0.7648 and 0.6050. Cutting communication reduces every restricted society to chance, and the depth-three advantage remains 0.558 on programs whose composite function never appeared in training. translated_title: 看不见的才是你学到的：受限证据可见性有利于共享基因组语言模型社会中的组合泛化
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.20054v1 公告类型：新 摘要：多模块系统通常将每个模块暴露于完整输入。我们测试了限制证据可见性是否会改变基于梯度的训练所发现的解决方案。四细胞社会共享一个冻结的预训练语言模型和一个低秩适配器，仅通过两个模型宽度的连续向量在固定中继中通信。在一个前瞻性密封的自然语言函数组合任务上，我们训练了十对匹配的受限/全局对，它们共享初始化字节、训练顺序、标记布局、参数和计算；仅注意力掩码不同。受限社会在9/10对中的两个深度上均优于其全局可见的孪生体至少20分，中位配对优势分别为0.7648和0.6050。削减通信使所有受限社会降至随机水平，且在复合函数从未出现在训练中的程序上，深度三优势仍为0.558。在六个审计的受限社会中...
tldr: 本研究通过限制模块间的证据可见性，显著提升了共享语言模型社会的组合泛化能力，表明信息遮挡能引导梯度训练发现更优解决方案。
en_tdlr: This study demonstrates that restricting evidence visibility between modules significantly improves compositional generalization in shared language-model societies, showing that information occlusion guides gradient-based training to discover superior solutions.
